title: eval-harness: add CI hook and gating for prompt-set regression checks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: add an automated CI hook that runs prompt-set regression checks as part of the eval-harness pipeline and fails the PR when quality regressions exceed project thresholds. This implements an infra-level quality gate that prevents accidental model or prompt regressions from being merged without an explicit triage.

What this change does: - Adds a new GitHub Actions job (eval/prompt-regression) that runs a lightweight eval harness subset against the affected prompt-sets. The job produces a compact report and a JSON metrics summary consumed by the gate. - Implements gating rules: fail if absolute drop in primary metric (e.g., exact-match or EM) is >= 1.0% relative to baseline, or if regression is observed on >= 2 prompt-sets for multi-set PRs. - Adds a helper CLI (eval-harness/tools/regression_gate.py) to compute diffs, apply smoothing, and produce human-readable summary. - Wire the gate into existing CI so that the eval job runs in parallel with unit/integration tests. A failing gate blocks squash-merge; maintainers can override with a DCO-approved bypass label.

Notes on design choices: - Thresholds are conservative by default; thresholds and strictness can be tuned via eval-harness/config/regression_gate.yaml per-repo. - The job runs only when files under eval-harness/prompt-sets/ or model-serving/changed, or when the PR has the label "run-eval-full". - To keep CI time bounded, the job runs a sampled subset of the full eval (10 prompts per set, cached base metrics on artifacts). For full diagnostics maintainers can trigger a longer job via the label.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement regression gate CLI and unit tests
- [x] Add GitHub Actions job and workflow config
- [x] Add config file with sane defaults and documentation
- [x] Add metrics summary artifact for downstream consumption
- [x] Update internal README with operational runbook and bypass instructions

Related: ENG-2148 (quality gating), ENG-2199 (eval infra stability), SUP-4321 (customer-reported prompt regression incident).

notes: This PR was motivated by SUP-4321 where a prompt-set regression slipped through due to missing gating. The gate is intentionally permissive to avoid blocking frequent small model churn while still catching regressions that impact production prompt-sets.
